story_title: Barley Yield Analysis: Performance Across Varieties and Sites (1931-1932)
story_subtitle: Exploring top-performing varieties, site-specific trends, and yield variations over two agricultural seasons

story_pieces.narration: Trebi and Wisconsin No. 38 achieved the highest yields, with Trebi reaching 65.77 units at Waseca in 1931—the highest recorded yield in the dataset—and Wisconsin No. 38 maintaining strong performance across multiple sites. These varieties exceeded the overall average yield of 34.42 units.
story_pieces.question: Which barley varieties achieved the highest yields, and how do they compare to the overall average?
story_pieces.visualization: ranked bar chart (variety vs. yield) with year filtering

story_pieces.narration: Sites such as Waseca and University Farm consistently produced higher yields, with Waseca averaging 44.3 units in 1931. In contrast, Grand Rapids and Duluth showed significantly lower yields, suggesting site-specific environmental factors affecting productivity.
story_pieces.question: How do different sites impact barley yield, and are there significant regional disparities?
story_pieces.visualization: grouped bar chart (site vs. yield) with year comparison

story_pieces.narration: From 1931 to 1932, most varieties experienced yield declines, with Manchuria and Svansota dropping by 20% in average yield. Trebi, however, demonstrated resilience, sustaining high yields despite the overall downward trend.
story_pieces.question: How did barley yields evolve over the two-year period, and which varieties were most resilient to yield fluctuations?
story_pieces.visualization: line chart (year vs. yield) with variety-specific lines

story_pieces.narration: Yield distribution across the dataset exhibits significant variability, with a standard deviation of 10.33 units. Outliers such as Glabron at Grand Rapids (14.43 units) and No. 462 at Grand Rapids (19.9 units) highlight extreme performance differences.
story_pieces.question: What is the spread of barley yields, and are there notable outliers or extreme values?

story_pieces.narration: Variety-site combinations significantly influence yield, with Trebi at Waseca (65.77 units) and Wisconsin No. 38 at Waseca (58.8 units) achieving the highest results. Conversely, Manchuria at Grand Rapids (22.13 units) and Glabron at Grand Rapids (14.43 units) represent the lowest yield combinations.
story_pieces.question: Which variety-site combinations yielded the highest and lowest results, and what patterns emerge from these extremes?
story_pieces.visualization: heatmap (variety vs. site) with yield intensity coloring
